title: Identify the Feasibility
statementMd:
Recently, Colin has been learning the relationship between sets and bitmasks. We can use binary numbers (bitmasks) to represent sets, and if some bits are 1 in the bitmask, then it means that the sets include the elements corresponding to the indices of these bits.

Now Colin has 𝑛n non-negative integers 𝑎1,𝑎2,⋯,𝑎𝑛a1,a2,⋯,an and all these integers are less than 2𝑘2k. Now Colin tries to use the concept of bitmasks and sets to understand the relationship between these integers.

For a non-negative integer 𝑥∈[0,2𝑘)x∈[0,2k), Colin defines that 𝑎𝑖ai is feasible with 𝑎𝑗aj under the augmentation of 𝑥x, if and only if the set corresponding to the bitmask 𝑎𝑖+𝑥ai+x is a subset of the set corresponding to the bitmask 𝑎𝑗+𝑥aj+x. Then Colin uses 𝑓(𝑥)f(x) to represent the number of all the pairs (𝑖,𝑗)(i,j) such that 𝑎𝑖ai is feasible with 𝑎𝑗aj under the augmentation of 𝑥x.

Now Colin would like to ask you to calculate the sum of all the 𝑓(𝑥)f(x), modulo 998244353998244353 .

Formally, please calculate

(∑𝑥=02𝑘−1𝑓(𝑥))mod998244353(∑x=02k−1f(x))mod998244353

## Input

The first line contains two integers 𝑛,𝑘 (1≤𝑛≤106,1≤𝑘≤20)n,k (1≤n≤106,1≤k≤20), representing the number of integers Colin has and all of these integers are less than 2𝑘2k.

The following line contains 𝑛n integers 𝑎1,𝑎2,⋯,𝑎𝑛(0≤𝑎𝑖<2𝑘)a1,a2,⋯,an(0≤ai<2k).

## Output

Output a single integer, representing the answer.

## Note

𝑓(0)=3:(1,1),(2,1),(2,2)f(0)=3:(1,1),(2,1),(2,2)

𝑓(1)=3:(1,1),(2,1),(2,2)f(1)=3:(1,1),(2,1),(2,2)

𝑓(2)=2:(1,1),(2,2)f(2)=2:(1,1),(2,2)

𝑓(3)=2:(1,1),(2,2)f(3)=2:(1,1),(2,2)
